newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business inventories rise sharply in October.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business inventories rise sharply in October.

text.p: Businesses added to inventories at the briskest rate in nine months during October, the Commerce Department said Friday, with retailers in particular adding stock before the Christmas sales season.

Total inventories held by manufacturers, retailers and wholesalers grew by 0.5 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted value of $1.01 trillion -- the biggest monthly increase since a 0.6 percent jump last January.
That followed a 0.1 percent addition to stocks of unsold goods during September. Wall Street economists had forecast only a 0.2 percent increase in October inventories.

The strong rate of inventory-building appears to signal optimism about future sales. Many goods now being sold in the critical Thanksgiving-to-Christmas holiday season were brought into inventories during October and earlier, especially imported consumer goods from China and elsewhere.
Overall business sales rose during October by 0.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted $724.2 billion after a 0.7 percent rise in September.
In October, inventories increased at all stages of business activity.
October retail inventories were built up by 0.7 percent to $314.8 billion after 0.6 percent gain in September. There were significant additions to stocks of clothing, food and furniture.
Manufacturers' inventories rose 0.3 percent to $437.9 billion and wholesalers' inventories grew 0.6 percent to $258.6 billion.
The inventory-to-sales ratio -- a measure of how long it would take to sell existing stocks at the current pace -- rose to 1.40 months' worth in October from 1.39 months in September.
